member.name: P:Lumio.GameRuntime.Ecs.AbilityTypeAttribute.Prediction
member.summary: Declared prediction intent. Documentary only: no runtime path dispatches on this value.
member.remarks:
The generator deliberately does not read it, so it reaches neither the generated ability registry nor AbilityTypeCatalog, and changing it changes no observable behaviour. It records for readers and reviewers what an ability is meant to do; it does not make it happen.
What actually decides whether a client predicts an ability is, in order: 1. whether the host opened a joint prediction session for that connection at all (WorldManager.InitializeJointPrediction plus a GAS GasJointPrediction driver); with no driver the client only ever applies authority. 2. what the ability's body does on the compile side it is built for. Prediction re-executes the whole input command on the predicted world (WorldManager.ExecuteJointInput) rather than consulting a per-ability kind, so the side-specific step is the per-side partial split (Ability.Client.cs / Ability.Server.cs, selected by LumioEcsSide): an ability with no client-side implementation of that partial hook stages nothing into the prediction session on a client build, whatever is declared here.
Making this value dispatch is a cross-repo public-contract change (it would alter what upstream Client and gameplay code does), so it needs an architecture-repo ADR first, not a local patch. See .spec/decisions/0009-prediction-kind-is-declarative-intent.md. Do not add a new WireCodec mapping for movement.

member.summary: membership-list events (ADR-119 决策 6). A field declared Scope.Claim names a sibling (its / ) as the list of observers currently holding the claim — a chest's Openers. The list itself never rides the wire (Scope.None); only its net effect on the fields it gates does: joining resends every one of those fields at its current full value tagged granted, applied with PostAttribute semantics (no Changed hook); leaving sends revoked with no value. An observer that already holds the claim keeps getting ordinary sync for those fields through the regular dirty-field pass (WorldManager.Visibility.cs step 4); this file only produces the join/leave edge, and the field-projection hook in WorldManager.Visibility.cs only calls into it and skips the edge's fields in the ordinary pass.
Single owner of the authoritative World and, on the client, its PredictedWorld clone.

Section partition records (ADR-119 决策 7–9). Residency moves are the host's step between two Ticks, like a snapshot restore (ADR-104): they are not structural orders, do not pass the commit phase, and what they change becomes visible in the next Tick's projection. Deciding when a Section unloads or loads is not done here.
Per-observer visibility table and per-connection Section subscription table (ADR-119 决策 3–5, ecs M6).

remarks.para: The visibility table is the only truth for what an observer is sent. Its key is (observer, connection generation): a new generation is a fresh handshake that starts from an empty table and a full census. Entering sends the current full visible values; entities outside the table get no field changes and no ClientRpcs; leaving is a left_aoi addressed to that observer only; terminated goes only to the observers whose table held the entity.

Ordinary CS entities are in every observer's table (the whole room, unchanged until the ecs M6 spatial view lands). Block entities () never are by distance: their entries are derived from the Section subscription table — subscribed means in view, released means left_aoi — and they are excluded from the admission census. The Section → block-entity view is re-derived from the committed binding table through at every projection; Runtime keeps no binding table.

Table changes fire the server-side / . Projection (tick.md phase 11) runs no business code, so the hooks of tick T run at the start of ApplyInputs (phase 3) of the next tick, before that tick's inputs.
